Published online:
    September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references July vote, Jackson Hole speech, June/July inflation trends
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Sept 15-16 Fed meeting, potential December hike
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Back-to-back hotter-than-expected inflation prints (core CPI +0.3% MoM, +2.4% YoY; headline 3.4%) combined with a strong PPI and oil above $100/barrel are putting heavy pressure on the Fed to hike at its September 15-16 meeting. Fed funds futures now price ~85% probability of a 25bp hike, up from ~70% pre-report. Chairman Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole language is seen as virtually binding the Fed to act. A minority view holds that core PCE may print a benign 0.2%, leaving the decision on a "knife's edge." Market consensus leans toward at least one hike next week and a second in December, with the Fed's policy rate currently at 3.50%-3.75%.
